notes:
Tier 1 (direct HTTP) only, no block encountered. robots.txt (https://housedoctor.com/robots.txt) has no Claude-specific disallow, just a general Shopify 'Allow: /' plus standard admin/checkout/filter-trap disallows -> proceeded. Site is Shopify. Pulled the full /collections.json (271 collections across 2 pages) and cross-checked against /sitemap_collections_1.xml (271 locs, identical set) to get the complete site-wide category taxonomy, then keyword-scanned title+handle for christmas/jul/xmas/halloween/easter/paaske/valentin/thanksgiv/nytaar/diwali/advent/fastelavn/mors-dag/fars-dag etc. Also checked the live mega-menu/drawer nav on the homepage (no Christmas/Easter link currently shown there -- it's Sept, off-season, and the nav is evidently swapped seasonally -- so absence from the current nav was NOT treated as proof of absence; the collections.json/sitemap taxonomy was used instead since it lists all published collections regardless of current nav placement). No Halloween, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, Diwali, or other Indian-festival collections exist anywhere in the 271-collection taxonomy -- only Christmas and Easter are present. IMPORTANT: collections.json 'products_count' proved inflated/unreliable for this store (matches prior project finding) -- e.g. handle 'christmas' reported 641 in the API but the actual rendered PLP ('ProductCount' Liquid element + live product-grid links) showed only 99. All qty values below therefore come from the rendered on-page product count (server-rendered '

N products

' element, cross-checked against actual distinct /products/ links in the grid HTML), fetched via the /en/ locale for clean English category names, not from the collections.json API count. Three Christmas-named collections found in the taxonomy were EXCLUDED as not genuine PLPs: 'christmas-2025' (Julekollektionen), 'meraki-christmas-2025', and 'christmas-serving' (Borddækning) -- all three render on a different template (PageFly 'all_collections' custom template, no ProductCount element, and the only '/products/' reference on each page is one identical placeholder/example ID '210940401' repeated across all three, i.e. no real product grid), unlike every other Christmas/Easter collection which uses the standard Dawn collection template with a real product grid and matching counts on both the da (default) and en locale. These 3 are effectively inactive/placeholder collections currently and were treated as legit-zero/not-a-real-PLP, not counted. The main 'Christmas' collection (handle 'christmas', 99 products) is the umbrella/parent: its rendered total (99) closely matches the sum of its labeled Christmas subcategories (32+36+3+20+1+6+6+1+1=106, near-equal allowing for tag overlap/timing), and every subcategory's products are a subset of the main collection's tag scope, so per the parent/subset rule it is recorded as a grouping row (qty null, link null) rather than double-counted alongside its children. Easter has no such umbrella collection -- 'hd-easter-ss25' and 'easter-2026' are two separate, non-overlapping, same-level Easter collections (13 vs 2 products, different product sets, both titled simply 'Easter' on-site) so both are kept as sibling rows with a distinguishing sub_category label. Never used r.jina.ai/proxy/cache/wayback; never crawled PDPs beyond spot-checking a handful of /products/ links already present in the fetched PLP HTML to validate real vs placeholder grids.
